speaker: Head Coach
quote_text:
Mikel, it was the earliest goal in the Community  Shield since 1968. What does that say about  
the alertness of your team to go in front so  early? Well, I’m obviously extremely happy with  
the performance, with the result and winning  the first trophy. We talked about the desire  
that we have to start the season and to  show ourselves how much we wanted it,  
and I certainly saw a lot of positive things  there against a top opponent. We often get,  
I think, obsessed with massive, mega-money  signings, but Christos Tzolis comes in and has an  
amazing start. What were your thoughts  on his game? Well, what I said last week,  
that I think he’s come into the team and really  organically he’s fitting in. He’s a really  
intelligent boy and he has a massive quality,  which is when he’s in the last 20, 30 metres,  
he’s so composed to pick people around the box or  to finish actions. And he’s shown that again two  
or three times, and he was decisive. A classic,  dominant performance from the very start of the  
game. How much of this is down to what happened  last season, in terms of you’re now champions,  
you’re now over that line after 20 years?  Psychologically, does that have an impact  
and help you today? I think it’s down to the  preparation that we’ve done in pre-season, to the  
decisions that the boys have taken after the World  Cup to continue to get prepared, to come early  
because they wanted to be part of this, and they  really wanted to win the competition because it’s  
something that we earned last year, the chance  to play against City here. And I’m very impressed  
with the manner that we played, especially in the  manner that we competed. So that’s the standard  
for us, and if we drive the standards at this  level, I’m sure that we’re going to be really,  
really competitive. But surely that has some  effect and some change, that you’re now champions?  
Surely. Probably there is more belief. You know  how to do it, you know what it takes to win it  
and the contribution of everybody. Because last  season, that was the biggest asset of the team,  
that every single player contributed to make us  champions. We know that that’s going to be exactly  
the same. Just on Christos Tzolis again. You said  he’s so ruthless in those last 30 metres. Can you  
coach that? Can he get even better? Well, that’s  a natural quality. He has better players around  
him. You put him in more and more situations, so  the volume is higher. With the level of quality  
he has, the numbers will be higher. He’s so  eager to learn, to improve, to practise. And  
it’s not a coincidence. He’s a really consistent  player in everything that he does. And yeah,  
really impressed with him. The midfield now,  there’s incredible depth and versatility to it.  
Merino said it was probably the best midfield  in the world the other day. Do you share that  
feeling? Do you believe it’s the best? The best  midfield for us, that’s for sure. And that’s why  
we have to make it that everybody complements,  with their qualities, the player next to them  
and that we have this variability, that diversity  with the qualities that we need in relation to  
the opponent. And today again, you’ve seen it.  We change it and we bring other qualities in  
different moments of the game. And that’s really  a strong thing to have. I’ll talk to you about  
desire because talent is one thing, skill is one  thing. There was a tackle from Bruno on Doku,  
there was a tackle from Gabriel on Doku and  then White denied Haaland, threw himself in  
front of him. Is that more of an indicator, or  does that hearten you more, that the desire is  
in there to go again? Tell us about the desire.  They are really good examples. The way the team  
tracks back is just unbelievable, especially  when fitness-wise you are not there. So you  
have to get there in a different way. And when you  put your soul and your heart into every action,  
that’s what happens. I talk about desire with the  composure and desire to have the ball that we have  
against a team that are really good in the way  they press. They are really good when they regain  
the ball, especially inside and the way they do  this transition. And to have that courage and  
that composure is only if you desire to do that in  the manner that we’ve done it today. And I’m very  
pleased with that. And is that just because you’ve  achieved something, it’s that willingness to go  
again? Because you want to go through it again.  You know, the desire comes. I want to live that  
moment again. I want to live other moments even  bigger than them. And we know what it’s going to  
take. We know the difficulty of the task. That’s  why we’ve never done it in this football club,  
to win it again. So we know that it’s going to  demand something special and we are ready for it.  
I’ll ask you about Riccardo Calafiori. Obviously,  the first goal in 25 seconds. Was there something  
you wanted from him, like attacking more and  more, being that agent of chaos like he was last  
season? I think he can be a total player. I mean,  we can ask him to occupy certain areas of the  
pitch and when he gets in and around the box, he  has this intuition, his timing to create goals, to  
score goals. But at the same time, we ask him, you  know, the defensive duties too, what he has to do.  
And we ask him because he’s capable of doing it,  he knows how to do it. And if we maintain him fit  
and available, and with that physical condition,  I mean, he’s a top player. What do you think he  
needs to improve compared to last season? Again,  more consistency in everything, in his habits,  
in his availability and his robustness in the  decisive actions in the game. That’s why we have  
to put the focus on him, because he is more than  capable of doing it. Martin Ødegaard missed quite  
a few games for you last season and struggled  to get a bit of rhythm. How encouraging was it  
seeing him today, kind of get back to that kind of  level where he just controlled it? Well, he missed  
five or six months for different things and it was  extremely difficult for him to get any momentum.  
So I’m sure this year, if we can maintain him  fit, available, with the players around him,  
we’re going to see a very different Martin. And I  sensed from the first day that he joined that he  
has something else in the belly that he wants to  prove and show because the team needs it as well.  
Hi, Mikel. Congratulations. You had to leave  some very good players out of the squad today,  
Gabriel Martinelli, Gabriel Jesus and more. Can  I ask, are those technical decisions or are they  
associated with the players? No, just technical  decisions. I’ve been trying to persuade the  
Premier League and the clubs, you know, to be able  to extend the number of players that we can have,  
especially the outfield players in the squads,  because we play more and more and the load is  
unreal. And to not give the chance to those  players to be able to be here, to participate,  
because maybe the game demands the qualities  of one of those players and you don’t have  
them available, it’s just a shame. So yeah, it’s  the most difficult part of the job, but there’s  
nothing to do with that. It’s just a fact that we  can bring 18 outfield players and we believe that  
for today’s game, these were the options that we  needed, especially with the physical condition  
of certain players. And in terms of the market,  a number of attacking players you had to leave  
out today, but only one defender on the bench.  Does that show maybe where the focus will be,  
the emphasis will be in what’s left of the window?  Well, we know that there are certain areas that  
through injuries we are weaker and we need to  strengthen. We are trying to do that. We’ve been  
trying to do that for weeks. So only if the right  opportunity and the club is available to do it,  
we will do it. Just coming back to Declan Rice, he  played 69 games last season for club and country.  
I mean, can he do that again, or are you going  to have to manage him slightly differently when  
Sam is talking about the strength you’ve got in  midfield? Well, he’s done it previously. You know,  
the last two or three seasons, he’s done something  very similar to that. So he’s already done it.  
Hopefully he doesn’t need to do it that  consistently and can focus more on the  
quality and the performance than the volume.  But probably he will say the opposite and he  
will say that he wants to play 70 this year if  he can, because he wants to go for everything.
title: Mikel Arteta on Community Shield victory and Arsenal transfer plans | Arsenal 3-0 Manchester City
